current.text: He is projected to start at power forward for Utah and to close some games at center.
Jaxson Hayes started at center in the preseason because Utah does not want Jackson playing much center.
Walker Kessler is gone from Utah.
Experts expect more minutes in Utah and a better season than last year. They say his new opportunity matters more than last season's production.
Kessler's exit may help his blocks. Josh does not expect 3 blocks per game, but thinks 2 per game is possible with less offensive usage.
His usage will likely drop, because he shares the ball with Lauri Markkanen, Keyonte George and Darryn Peterson. He is not expected to reach his Memphis career-high numbers.
Leaf expects his easiest baskets in years, slipping screens while defenses chase Markkanen.
The experts disagree on his rebounding upside. Leaf projects a double-double, while Josh says 10 rebounds per game would be a huge outcome.
Utah is trying to win this season and is not expected to tank or shut players down.
Experts call him undervalued. He is good value at Yahoo ADP 55, too low at ESPN 82, and ranks about 36th in category leagues, so he is a target about two rounds after his ADP.
In a 9-cat mock draft he went in round 4 to a team built around blocks with poor assists.

durable.text: He is one of very few bigs who can block two shots and score 20 points per game.
Blocks are his clear outlier category, far above the top 250 pool.
Turnovers are high for a forward or center, so the TO category is his weak spot.
He is a poor rebounder for a big man.
His blocks have been declining over recent seasons.
He is not a good passer.
He has not been able to play center over the last 4 to 5 years and plays best next to a big, physical center.
He is usually worth more in category leagues than in points leagues.

note: He went for 29 USD in our league last season. Yahoo values him at 25 USD but his average cost is only 15.3 USD, and ESPN prices him near 6 USD. Experts rank him about 36th in categories, so anything in the high teens is a strong buy, and up to the mid 20s is fair. He fits blocks-first and punt TO builds, while his weak rebounding and poor passing lean toward punt AST teams. Early in the season, check whether he gets more than 30 minutes, how often he plays center next to Hayes or Nurkic, and whether his blocks climb toward 2 per game.
